title: Independent Affine Comparison Bound
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $A,D,U,V\colon\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be measurable up to null sets, with the pair $(A,D)$ also measurable up to null sets. Suppose $U$ and $V$ are each independent of $(A,D)$. Let $\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, and suppose $\psi(A+DU)$ and $\psi(A+DV)$ are integrable. Let $B\colon\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $B(A,D)$ integrable, and suppose for every $(a,d)\in\mathbb R^2$ that $\left|\mathbb E[\psi(a+dU)]-\mathbb E[\psi(a+dV)]\right|\le B(a,d)$. Then $\left|\mathbb E[\psi(A+DU)]-\mathbb E[\psi(A+DV)]\right|\le\mathbb E[B(A,D)]$.
hypotheses_covered: $(A,D)$ is measurable up to null sets
$U$ is measurable up to null sets
$V$ is measurable up to null sets
